source_text: His ita de prologo digestis, videamus iam etiam quae sequuntur in ipso corpore libelli. Incipit: Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui. Meminisse oportet quod in praefatione praemonuimus, quia libellus hic epithalamii habens speciem dramatis in modum conscribitur. Secundum hanc speciem historica a nobis aptabitur expositio; spiritalis vero intelligentia in sequentibus Libris, Domino praestante, pandetur.
pass_a_gloss: With-these thus about prologue having-been-digested, let-us-see already also which follow in itself body of-little-book. It-begins: Let-him-kiss me from kisses of-mouth of-him. To-remember it-behooves that in preface we-forewarned...
pass_b_english: With the prologue thus set out, let us now look also at what follows in the body of the little book itself. It begins: [[Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]]. We must remember what we warned in the preface: this little book, having the appearance of an epithalamium, is written in the manner of a drama. According to that form a historical exposition will be fitted by us; but the spiritual understanding will, the Lord granting, be opened in the Books that follow.
